title: Parking cash for days
summary: Money market tools lend for very short periods, so cash stays easy to reach with modest, not zero, risk.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Meera has ₹20,000 of virtual play money she may need within a few weeks. A **money market** fund in this example lends to borrowers for very short periods, from one day up to about a year, such as a fictional lender called Lotus Credit Ltd.

Because loans end quickly, the money comes back soon. This gives high **liquidity**: you can usually get your cash out in a day or two. It is not instant for every product, so check the **exit time** and any **exit charge**.

Returns here are assumed at 6% a year, an assumption for this example, not a promise. Short loans still carry some risk. If a borrower is late in paying, the value can dip, and when interest rates change, the return changes too. Past returns do not guarantee future ones.

What to check: how long the loans last, who the borrowers are, and how fast you can withdraw. Higher return usually means higher risk. Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: A money market fund mostly lends money for:

options.text: Very short periods, up to about a year

questions.explanation: Money market instruments are short-term loans, from a day up to about a year.

questions.prompt: Why is a money market fund called highly liquid?

options.text: Loans end soon, so cash usually comes back quickly

questions.explanation: Liquidity means how quickly you can turn money back into cash; short loans help, but check exit time.
